title: Ticketing beyond the gate: opening the way to a better guest experience
summary:
From the parking lot to the final attraction, every point of entry shapes the guest experience.

Modern ticketing access solutions do more than speed up lines - they enhance safety, improve staffing efficiency, and deliver a smoother, more memorable visit.

Whether you're building a new park or modernizing an existing space, integrating self-scanning technology early in the planning process ensures your operations are ready for the future.

Flexible, scalable, and proven across attractions, water parks, zoos, and fairs, these systems help you design a guest journey that starts and ends with ease.

​1. Venue entry


The moment guests arrive, efficiency and ease set the stage for their entire experience.

Self-scanning ticket technology helps achieve both by shifting staff attention from ticket collection to genuine guest interaction. Portable wireless options offer flexibility for smaller or seasonal venues, while fixed installations deliver reliability for larger, year-round operations.

Modern scanners that accept printed and digital barcodes, RFID, and NFC media ensure the entry process evolves alongside guest preferences.

Just as important, solutions with proven integration to leading ticketing platforms simplify deployment - creating a true plug-and-play system that keeps lines moving and guests smiling from the start.

​2. Attractions


Once inside the park, guests expect their experience to flow as smoothly as their entry.

Many ticketing options now include faster line access or premium entry privileges, and self-scanning solutions make these benefits easy to redeem right at the attraction.

Portable wireless scanners add flexibility, allowing staff to position fast-lane access points wherever demand is highest - closer to or farther from the attraction as needed.


In addition to improving convenience, these systems can also support patron counting and flow management, giving operators real-time insights to balance efficiency, safety, and guest satisfaction throughout the day.

​3. Exhibits


Beyond rides and slides, many venues feature exhibits that add depth and discovery to the guest experience - from aquariums and zoos to seasonal festivals, educational displays, and in-venue theaters.

Integrating self-scanning technology at exhibit entrances allows for seamless access control, whether tickets grant VIP privileges or include separate admission fees. These systems also simplify patron counting, helping operators maintain comfort and safety by tracking capacity in real time.

The result is a smoother, more flexible entry process that enhances both the guest journey and operational efficiency, ensuring each exhibit visit feels as effortless as it is engaging.

​4. Guest parking


A smooth parking experience sets the tone before guests ever reach the gate. For many, parking feels like a chore, but self-scanning technology helps make it a seamless start to the day.


When integrated with automatic gates, dedicated self-scan lanes allow guests who prepaid or hold season passes to bypass long payment lines entirely. These systems also support flexible access options - from single-day parking to passholder privileges - while reducing the need for staffed kiosks.

Fewer on-site transactions mean teams can focus on directing traffic efficiently, creating a faster, less stressful arrival for every guest.

​5. Employee entry


Guests aren't the only ones who need smooth access each day. From ride operators to food service teams, employees also require a safe, efficient, and reliable way to enter the venue.

Larger parks often benefit from dedicated staff entry points equipped with secure access control systems that integrate directly with employee credentials.

Smaller or seasonal venues, however, may find it more practical for staff to enter through guest gates using scanners that can also validate employee passes.

Both approaches streamline daily operations, strengthen security, and ensure the entry experience is just as seamless behind the scenes as it is for guests.

title: Six Flags Magic Mountain's new solar carport starts generating clean energy
summary:
Six Flags Magic Mountain has announced that its solar carport project is now operational and producing electricity.

The largest solar carport installation in California is designed to offset 100 percent of the annual electricity consumption of Six Flags Magic Mountain and Hurricane Harbor Los Angeles.

Developed in partnership with Solar Optimum and local community and government officials, the 12.37-megawatt installation is one of the largest single-site commercial solar carport projects in the US.

"This is a transformative moment for Six Flags Magic Mountain and our sustainability journey," said Brian Oerding, park president of Six Flags Magic Mountain.

A new solar carport installation is designed to offset 100% of the annual electricity consumption of Six Flags Magic Mountain Six Flags

"By investing in renewable energy, we're taking meaningful action to reduce our environmental impact while helping build a more sustainable future for our guests, team members and community.

"This project demonstrates what's possible when organizations commit to innovation and responsible environmental stewardship."

The installation will generate approximately 20.8 million kilowatt-hours of clean electricity annually, as well as providing coverage for around 4,315 parking spaces.

The project is expected to deliver environmental benefits equivalent to eliminating more than 8,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, conserving more than 10 million gallons of water each year, or removing 3,182 gasoline-powered vehicles from the roads.

Sustainability at Six Flags

"We are proud to celebrate the energization of this extraordinary project with Six Flags,” said Arno Aghamalian, CEO of Solar Optimum.

"This system demonstrates how innovative renewable energy solutions can help organizations meet ambitious sustainability goals while delivering long-term environmental and economic benefits.

"Together, we're creating a cleaner energy future for generations to come."

Six Flags Magic Mountain said the solar carport project is advancing its sustainability objectives while setting a new benchmark for renewable energy deployment within the attractions industry.

title: Mattel unveils first immersive water park, opening in Nebraska in 2027
summary:
Mattel has unveiled its immersive water park concept in new renderings, and confirmed its first attraction will open in Bellevue, Nebraska at the end of 2027.

Designed as a year-round, multi-brand destination, the approximately 100,000-square-foot water park is inspired by Mattel brands such as Barbie, Hot Wheels, UNO and more.

"Mattel Wonder Indoor Waterparks are about bringing great experiences to where our fans actually live," said Natalia Premovic, chief consumer products and experiences officer at Mattel.

Mattel's new water park is inspired by brands such as Barbie, Hot Wheels, UNO and moreMartin Aquatic

"We see a real opportunity to take the kind of immersive entertainment traditionally concentrated in major markets and bring it to more communities in a scalable, year-round format," she added.

"Bellevue becoming our first water park to open is an important step in that strategy and a significant chance to show what happens when you bring so many of our brands together in one place."

Construction on the Bellevue location is underway, and Mattel has also confirmed water parks for Orlando, Florida; Bradley, Illinois; and Roanoke Rapids, North Carolina.

Experiences coming to Bellevue include a Barbie activity pool, a Hot Wheels multi-slide tower, and a lazy river inspired by UNO, Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots and Magic 8 Ball.

Experiences coming to Mattel's water park in Bellevue include a Barbie activity poolMartin Aquatic

Highlights also include a Fisher-Price water play structure, as well as themed F&B offerings.

Mattel's water parks are being developed in partnership with water park management company American Resort Management and aquatic design firm Martin Aquatic.

American Resort Management will oversee the water parks' daily performance and guest-flow optimisation.

“Seeing the building take shape is exciting, but the interior is where the vision will really come to life,” said Rick Coleman, CEO of American Resort Management.

The Mattel Wonder Indoor Waterpark is designed as a year-round, multi-brand destinationMartin Aquatic

“Our goal is to create an experience that feels unmistakably Mattel while delivering the quality, service and guest experience families expect from a world-class waterpark.”

Earlier this year, WhiteWater was named the exclusive global water attraction vendor for all future Mattel Wonder Indoor Waterparks.

OpenAire has also partnered with American Resort Management on the Mattel water parks project.
